locator: §5.2, 'Success would leave us with no way to distinguish plausible non-cognitivism from cognitivism.'
interpretation: The collapse argument (creeping minimalism: Boghossian, Wright, Divers and Miller; Dreier 2004b): if minimalism about truth conditions and belief carries the whole quasi-realist program, the quasi-realist can no longer claim that moral judgments are not truth-apt and not beliefs. The quasi-realist regroups by contrasting minimal with robust truth, truth-conditionality and belief (Blackburn 2006; Sinclair; McDonald). This is the informal form of the collapse lemma, recorded as support for it, not as a premise. Attribution reading on a secondary witness: the claim records the position the entry reports, not a thesis of the entry's author. No primary text is pinnable (in copyright, no immutable open text).
